$comment: What the package-schema acceptance criterion answers on this tree, per assertion (D-110).
A two-way ratchet: the CI job fails when a run disagrees with this file in either direction.
Six of the nine are `fail` today and are supposed to be — a package still cannot ship SCHEMA
until feature 080's Wave 3 finishes. Recording that is what makes an accidental *green* as
visible as an accidental red: a change that quietly satisfied A4 without going through the
composition would show up here as drift, not as a pass nobody looked at.
Move an entry only in the merge request that earned the move, and never to make a pipeline
pass. When Wave 3 lands, every entry becomes `pass` and this file becomes the guard against
regressions rather than the record of a gap.
T031 moved A5 to `pass` (an installed package now reaches `resolvedManifestEntries()` and
both composition roots) and corrected A6's and A7's reasons, which had both read `Follows
A5` and stopped being true the moment A5 did.

A1.reason: The migration registry is emitted by a filesystem walk of `backend/src` (`generate-composer.ts`) and committed. A package contributes no entry, so its migration class is never handed to the migrator and never lands in `mikro_orm_migrations`. Closed by Wave 3 T033 (P3, merged `orderMigrations` inputs).

A2.reason: Follows A1: no migration ran, so the table does not exist.

A3.reason: Follows A1. It is kept separate from A2 on purpose — when A2 first goes green it must be because the body ran, not because a row was written.

A4.reason: The entity registry is emitted from a source-text probe for `@Entity(` under `backend/src` (`generate-composer.ts:603`), and compilation turns the decorator into `__decorate([...])`. A published package therefore contributes zero entities and the ORM metadata has no `AcceptanceProbeRow`. Closed by Wave 3 T033.

A5.reason: Earned by T031 (P1) plus the smallest slice of T032 the assertion forces. `loadPackageModuleEntries` (`src/packages/`) enumerates the instance's `node_modules`, keeps every package carrying `endora.type === "module"` whose install does not link out of the tree it was found under, and both composition roots now call `composeModules([...MODULES, ...overlay, ...packages], …)`. `resolvedManifestEntries()` merges the same discovery, so the module has an identity, its permission is grantable and the palette action resolves in `en` and `pl`. The T032 slice is `filePath`: it is the resolved `package.json`, because `dirname(filePath)` is how the i18n reconciler and the orchestrator find a module's assets and the compiled root export's directory holds no `i18n/`. What is still T032's: nothing here loads a package's bundles through the platform's own reconciler — A5 reads them through `loadModuleBundles` at the path this entry reports.

A6.reason: No longer `follows A5` — the module is in the resolved set since T031, and this is still red for two reasons of its own. (1) `composition.ts` reconciles settings from `collectRegisteredSettingsManifests(REGISTERED_MANIFESTS)`, the bare-core registry, which is stated in its own comment as a deliberate cut; so a package's (and an overlay's) `settings` manifest reaches no reconciler and the activation row is never created. (2) The probe's `gate-off` phase reads the row before it composes anything, and no earlier phase composes the application, so on a fresh database no reconciler has run at all. Fixing (1) alone moves nothing, which is why it is not fixed here. Belongs with T032/T033, where the merged registry gets an owner (D-155.3(c)).

A7.reason: No longer `follows A5`, and the failure moved: the orchestrator now finds `acceptance_probe` in the registry and runs the hard uninstall, which answers `reverted 0 migration(s); migration row gone; table dropped`. It reverts nothing because there is nothing to revert — the package's migration never ran (A1) — so this closes with T033 and not before. The three-part detail is what makes that readable: two thirds of A7 are already true and only the count is not.

A8.reason: Passes today, and must: it measures the harness, not the platform. The tarball install resolves entirely inside the throwaway instance. An A8 that could not pass before Wave 3 would be an assertion nobody could trust after it.

A9.reason: Passes today, and must, for the same reason: A8 refuses the same package consumed by link from inside this repository. If A9 ever fails, A8 has stopped being able to say no and every other assertion is worth less.
